question: On what grounds is mahāmāyā posited as threefold, with one form being gross and consisting of the guṇas?
premises: Mahāmāyā is posited as a single entity capable of division.
A threefold division of it is proposed.
One of those forms is gross and consists of the guṇas.
inference: Mahāmāyā may be threefold, and in that division one form is gross and consists of the guṇas.
uncertainties: The other two forms of the threefold division are not specified in this verse.
plain_english: Mahāmāyā may be threefold; there, one form is gross and consists of the guṇas.
